title: Durotar
body: Durotar is a hard country of red rock and baking heat on the eastern shore of Kalimdor, the homeland Thrall claimed for the orcs after the battle at Mount Hyjal and named for his father, Durotan. Its capital, Orgrimmar, rises in the northern mountains. The land was not empty: Razormane quilboar and Kolkar centaurs still lurk in it, Kul Tiran soldiers hold a keep on the coast, and the demon cult of the Burning Blade hides in its caves. The Darkspear trolls share it from Sen'jin Village.

title: Valley of Trials
body: Hemmed in by red cliffs in the south of Durotar, the Valley of Trials is where young orcs and trolls come of age, sent out from the Den at its heart against boars and scorpids. Even this proving ground is not clean. In the caves of the northern cliffs the Burning Blade has made a coven, and its imps and felstalkers spill out into the valley, a warning that the cult has wider designs on Durotar.

title: Spirit Rock and the Shrine of the Dormant Flame
body: Two holy places of the Horde's shaman stand in Durotar. Spirit Rock lies at the end of the Hidden Path southwest of the Valley of Trials, and on one of the highest peaks above the Southfury River stands the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, which treasure hunters climb to and leave thinking empty. A novice who drinks a sapta, a draught that binds the spirit to an element, in such a place sees what others cannot.

parts.body: At Spirit Rock the earth itself stands revealed, a living presence that asks only humility of the novice: the mountains will be their strength, the plains their patience.
sources: quest 1517 description (Spirit Rock southwest of Canaga, end of the Hidden Path, sapta drunk only in a holy place)

parts.body: At the shrine the secret is fire: a manifestation of flame that grows stronger the longer it is left to fight, and whose embers kindle a white hot flame in the shrine's brazier.

title: Sen'jin Village
body: When the witch doctor Zalazane turned his voodoo on his own tribe, the free Darkspear trolls left the Echo Isles off Durotar's southern coast and built Sen'jin Village on the strand, naming it for Vol'jin's father. Zalazane still rules the largest isle among trolls he has hexed and bound to his will, and his tainted fetishes foul the flow of magic across the land. In the village the old witch doctor Master Gadrin speaks for the tribe.

parts.body: Zalazane's head was laid before Gadrin, and to the old witch doctor it meant the reign of evil was over: the tribe could sleep in peace again.

title: Razor Hill
body: Razor Hill stands at the crossroads of central Durotar under Gar'Thok, who survived a Kul Tiran massacre at an orc outpost in the first days of Durotar and has not forgotten it. Soon after the orcs came, Kul Tiran agents lured Thrall to a false parley here, and Rexxar went in his stead. Orgnil Soulscar polices the land against the Burning Blade from here, and recruits from the Valley pass through on their way into the wider land.

title: Tiragarde Keep
body: Admiral Daelin Proudmoore built this keep on Durotar's eastern coast when he brought the fleet of Kul Tiras against the orcs. The Horde broke his offensive and the admiral died at Theramore, but his reserves under Lieutenant Benedict came back and retook the keep. To the orcs it is a splinter in their homeland, and proof that the pact Thrall made with Jaina Proudmoore did not bind her father's men.

parts.body: Benedict's chest held orders under the admiral's own seal: Proudmoore's plans were laid well before his death, and more of his ships may yet come.

title: Razormane Grounds and Kolkar Crag
body: When the orcs came, the Razormane quilboar held much of Durotar, and though most have been driven out, their fortified camps still cling to the bramble-covered hills west of Razor Hill. Over the ridge from Sen'jin, at Kolkar Crag, Kolkar centaurs have pitched a camp of their own under Warlord Kolkanis, and the trolls of the village keep a wary watch on their western flank.

title: Skull Rock
body: Skull Rock is a cave in the mountains just east of Orgrimmar, and it shelters the largest band of the Burning Blade in Durotar. Within, under the orc warlock Gazz'uz, the cultists perform their rites and burn their own flesh with searing collars that seem to attune them to demonic power, a rebellion festering on the doorstep of the capital.

parts.body: Gazz'uz carried a pendant through which an unseen voice demanded his report, and threatened that if he would not speak, Neeru Fireblade would learn of him.
